front: What was the Battle of Marathon (490 BC)?
back: A decisive Greek victory over the Persian Empire on the plains of Marathon, preserving Greek independence and inspiring the legend of Pheidippides' run to Athens

front: What was the Battle of Thermopylae (480 BC)?
back: A famous last stand where 300 Spartans and allied Greeks held off the massive Persian army of Xerxes I at a narrow coastal pass for three days

front: What was the Battle of Salamis (480 BC)?
back: A naval battle where the outnumbered Greek fleet defeated the Persian navy in the straits near Athens, turning the tide of the Greco-Persian Wars

front: What was the Battle of Gaugamela (331 BC)?
back: Alexander the Great's decisive victory over Persian King Darius III, effectively ending the Achaemenid Empire and making Alexander ruler of Persia

front: What was the Battle of Cannae (216 BC)?
back: Hannibal's masterpiece of tactical warfare where Carthaginian forces encircled and destroyed a much larger Roman army, killing up to 70,000 Romans in a single day

front: What was the Battle of Alesia (52 BC)?
back: Julius Caesar's siege of the Gallic stronghold where he built double fortifications — one facing in and one facing out — defeating Vercingetorix and completing the Roman conquest of Gaul

front: What was the Battle of Actium (31 BC)?
back: A naval battle where Octavian defeated the combined forces of Mark Antony and Cleopatra, leading to the end of the Roman Republic and the rise of the Roman Empire

front: What was the Battle of Teutoburg Forest (9 AD)?
back: Germanic tribes under Arminius ambushed and destroyed three Roman legions, permanently halting Roman expansion east of the Rhine River

front: What was the Battle of Tours (732 AD)?
back: Frankish leader Charles Martel defeated an invading Umayyad Muslim army in central France, often credited with halting the Islamic advance into Western Europe

front: What was the Battle of Hastings (1066)?
back: William the Conqueror's Norman forces defeated King Harold II of England, fundamentally changing English culture, language, and governance

front: What was the Battle of Hattin (1187)?
back: Saladin's decisive victory over the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem, leading to the Muslim recapture of Jerusalem and triggering the Third Crusade

front: What was the Battle of Agincourt (1415)?
back: English King Henry V's outnumbered army, relying heavily on longbowmen, defeated a much larger French force during the Hundred Years' War

front: What was the Fall of Constantinople (1453)?
back: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II captured the Byzantine capital using massive cannons, ending the 1,000-year Byzantine Empire and marking the end of the medieval era

front: What was the Battle of Lepanto (1571)?
back: A Holy League fleet defeated the Ottoman navy in the largest naval battle in Western history since antiquity, checking Ottoman expansion in the Mediterranean

front: What was the Spanish Armada (1588)?
back: The failed invasion fleet sent by Spain's Philip II against England, defeated by English ships and devastating storms, shifting naval power toward England

front: What was the Battle of Vienna (1683)?
back: A combined European force led by Polish King Jan III Sobieski defeated the Ottoman siege of Vienna, marking the beginning of Ottoman decline in Europe

front: What was the Battle of Blenheim (1704)?
back: The Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy defeated a Franco-Bavarian army, preventing French domination of Europe during the War of the Spanish Succession

front: What was the Battle of Trafalgar (1805)?
back: Admiral Horatio Nelson's Royal Navy destroyed the combined French and Spanish fleet, securing British naval supremacy for over a century, though Nelson was killed

front: What was the Battle of Austerlitz (1805)?
back: Napoleon's greatest victory, where he defeated a larger Russo-Austrian army through brilliant tactical deception, also known as the Battle of the Three Emperors

front: What was the Battle of Waterloo (1815)?
back: Napoleon's final defeat by the Duke of Wellington and Prussian forces under Blücher in Belgium, ending the Napoleonic era and reshaping European politics

front: What was the Battle of Gettysburg (1863)?
back: The bloodiest battle of the American Civil War, a decisive Union victory in Pennsylvania that marked the turning point against the Confederacy

front: What was the Battle of Tsushima (1905)?
back: The Japanese navy destroyed the Russian Baltic Fleet in the strait between Korea and Japan, the first modern victory of an Asian power over a European one

front: What was the Battle of the Somme (1916)?
back: One of the bloodiest battles of WWI, with over 1 million casualties over nearly five months. The British suffered 57,000 casualties on the first day alone

front: What was the Battle of Verdun (1916)?
back: A 10-month WWI battle of attrition between French and German forces, becoming a symbol of French determination with the motto 'They shall not pass'

front: What was the Battle of Stalingrad (1942-1943)?
back: The turning point of WWII's Eastern Front, where the Soviet Union encircled and destroyed Germany's 6th Army after months of brutal urban warfare

front: What was the Battle of Midway (1942)?
back: A pivotal WWII naval battle where the US Navy sank four Japanese aircraft carriers, shifting the balance of power in the Pacific Theater

front: What was D-Day / Battle of Normandy (1944)?
back: The largest amphibious invasion in history, where Allied forces landed on five beaches in Normandy, France, beginning the liberation of Western Europe from Nazi control

front: What was the Battle of the Bulge (1944-1945)?
back: Germany's last major offensive on the Western Front, a surprise attack through the Ardennes forest that initially pushed back Allied lines before being defeated

front: What was the Battle of Berlin (1945)?
back: The final major battle in Europe during WWII, where Soviet forces captured the German capital, leading to Hitler's suicide and Germany's unconditional surrender

front: What was the Battle of Dien Bien Phu (1954)?
back: A Viet Minh victory over French colonial forces in Vietnam, ending French rule in Indochina and setting the stage for American involvement in Vietnam
